title: Election Day in America: Voters Decide Control of Congress in Trump Referendum
excerpt: Polls are open across the United States on Tuesday, November 3, with all 435 House seats, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships on the ballot — and narrow Republican majorities in both chambers at stake.
body:
• Americans are voting on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, in midterm elections that will decide control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump's term.
  • All 435 House seats, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships are on the ballot. Republicans hold the House 218-214 and the Senate 53-47, so Democrats need a net gain of four seats in each chamber to take control.
  • More than 50 million ballots were cast early or by mail before Election Day, according to The Sun's tally of early voting.
  • Still to vote? Most polling places open between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and close between 7 p.m. and 8 p.m. local time, and if you are in line when polls close you are still entitled to vote. Find your assigned polling place through USA.gov.

Americans are heading to the polls on Tuesday in midterm elections that will decide control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump's term, according to Reuters. The results will serve as the first nationwide verdict on Trump's presidency, revealing whether voters want to check the Republican president's power by giving Democrats control of one or both chambers of Congress, or are willing to accept the status quo despite frustrations over the cost of living and the US-led war with Iran.

What is being decided today

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are up for election, alongside governors in 36 states and a long list of state and local offices. Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the House and the Senate to overturn Republicans' narrow 218-214 and 53-47 majorities, Reuters reported. Democrats are widely expected to reclaim the House, but the Senate battle remains highly competitive: the close Senate fight will likely hinge on six to eight races, and Democrats need to flip several Republican-held seats in states Trump carried by double-digit margins in 2024, including Ohio, Iowa, Alaska and Texas. Even Kansas, despite Trump's 16-point win there in 2024, has become competitive in recent weeks. Republicans can retain control of the Senate by winning most of those contests, while Democrats will likely need to hold Michigan and pick up Maine.

Turnout, and what to watch at the polls

More than 50 million Americans had already cast ballots early or by mail before Election Day, The Sun reported. Opinion polls showed Democrats significantly more enthusiastic about voting than Republicans heading into Election Day, according to Reuters, although strategists caution that Democratic constituencies including young, Black and Hispanic voters have historically turned out at lower rates in midterm elections than in presidential years. Republicans argue that many of their supporters traditionally wait until Election Day to vote. Most polling places open between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and close between 7 p.m. and 8 p.m., The Sun reported, and voters who are in line at closing time are still entitled to cast a ballot. Your polling place is assigned by your home address; USA.gov's polling place finder points voters to their state or local election office to confirm their location and hours.

The disputes that could follow the count

Election officials have warned that close races could spark disputes over voter eligibility, ballot counting and certification, while long lines, machine malfunctions or challenges by partisan poll watchers could fuel litigation and delay results, Reuters reported. Trump's Justice Department plans to deploy about 1,000 monitors nationwide on Election Day, roughly triple the number used in the last midterms — a move some local officials worry could intimidate voters, although the department says those fears are baseless. On October 22, the Justice Department sued to preemptively block Alaska from certifying the results of its Senate race if the Republican incumbent loses by a narrow margin. Several states are also unlikely to produce complete results on election night, especially in close races.

What the result will set in motion

Democratic wins in one or both chambers will likely trigger investigations into the ethics of Trump and his administration, and into their handling of immigration enforcement and the Iran war, according to Reuters — questions that reach directly into issues Indian-American voters have followed closely this cycle, from H-1B policy to enforcement operations. A stronger-than-expected Republican showing could reinforce Trump's grip on his party, while heavy losses could increase pressure to rethink unpopular policies such as tariffs and the war. Early results from Republican-held House seats in Florida and Virginia could provide the first clues to the size of any Democratic gains once polls begin closing this evening.
